problem: Existing navigational world models (PathDreamer, DREAMWALKER, Navigation World Models) rely on discrete state dynamics, static pretrained models, and costly pixel-level future prediction, so they neither model continuous action-state transitions nor adapt online to novel VLN-CE environments.
motivation: VLN agents must predict the outcomes of their actions and adapt to distribution shift in unseen environments. Existing world models are trained only in a pre-training stage and cannot update during deployment. Gradient-based test-time adaptation is slow and unstable, so the paper looks for a lightweight forward-update memory inside an RSSM.
key_idea: Build an RSSM-style latent world model for VLN-CE with a World-aware Navigator and a Foresight Action Planner, and add a Contextual Evolution Memory (CEM) that is updated by forward moving-average updates during both training and online testing, giving the agent foresight and self-evolution.
insight: Most of the gain comes from the world model itself: without self-evolution (w/o SE), R2R-CE val-unseen SR goes 43.77 to 46.87, and online evolution adds a further 1.04 (to 47.91). CEM beats an LSTM recurrent module (SR 47.91 vs 43.67) at nearly the base inference time (21.22s vs 20.53s), while gradient-based TTA methods (Tent, NOTE, SAR, ViDA, FSTTA) give little or negative gains. Adding an action embedding alone (Base-AE) gives no gain, so the improvement comes from latent dynamics modeling, and every loss term (reconstruction, action, KL) contributes.
method: World-aware Navigator (inference network): a visual encoder and RSSM with deterministic history h_t and stochastic state s_t; the Gaussian posterior q(s_t|h_t,a_{t-1},x_t) is parameterized by MLPs; action = delta position embedded linearly.

Contextual Evolution Memory (CEM): N_m learnable scene-context vectors; retrieves top-K by cosine similarity and blends them into h_t as h~=(1-alpha)h+alpha*sum mu_k v_k; retrieved entries are updated by forward moving average v_k<-(1-beta)v_k+beta*h_t, with no backprop, during training and online testing.

Foresight Action Planner (predictive network): rolls out T_p future steps in latent space with the shared recurrent module, a prior over s, a policy that predicts actions and a visual decoder that reconstructs visual embeddings (not pixels).

Pre-training objective: L_W = embedding reconstruction + action prediction (with NDTW regularization and L2 on delta position) + gamma*KL(posterior||prior) over observed T and predicted T_p steps; total loss L = L_W + L_IL (DAgger-style imitation of the base model).
Plug-in usage: applied to base VLN-CE agents (VLN-3DFF for monocular; ETPNav and HNR for panoramic); T_p=2, N_m=1000 by default; adds 2.30M parameters to a 228.96M base model.

setting.backbone: VLN-3DFF (monocular), ETPNav and HNR (panoramic) base models plus the NavMorph RSSM world model and CEM (trained)
setting.model_size: CEM adds 2.30M parameters to a 228.96M base model
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE training splits (with the base models' own training data); no extra web or synthetic data mentioned
setting.observation: monocular RGB-D sequence (VLN-3DFF) or panoramic RGB-D (12 views at 30° intervals)
setting.action_space: waypoint prediction converted into low-level controls (forward 0.25m, turn 15°, stop) in Habitat
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT actions used only in training)

numbers.extra: monocular RGB-D; online adaptation with batch size 1

The R2R-CE monocular test-unseen NE is printed as 6.01 in the main table but 6.11 in one draft table. The HNR-based RxR-CE NE is printed as 5.70 in the main table and 5.67 in the full table. Ablation tables use R2R-CE val-unseen and are not listed here.
results: NavMorph improves every base model it is plugged into. On R2R-CE val-unseen with monocular VLN-3DFF, SR rises from 43.8 to 47.9 and SPL from 29.4 to 33.2, while trajectory length drops from 26.16 to 22.54. With the panoramic HNR base, SR is 64 and SPL 53 on val-unseen, and SR 60 on test-unseen (HNR reproduced: 61 and 58). On RxR-CE val-unseen, SR is 30.76 (monocular) and 58.02 (panoramic, HNR base).
limitations: Gains on strong panoramic bases are modest (about 1-3 SR points), and results depend on the base model.
Imagined rollouts occasionally pass through walls or furniture, because the world model receives no environmental or navigation-reward feedback.
The memory size N_m and the number of predictive steps T_p are sensitive hyperparameters (results are non-monotonic in both); only simulator evaluation, with no real-robot tests.
